tea instead of coffee: My grandfather drinks hot tea instead of coffee every morning because coffee makes his heart beat too fast.
我爺爺每天早上以茶代替咖啡，因為咖啡會讓他心跳太快。
instead（放句首或句尾）: The store did not have the red shoes in my size, so I bought a pair of white ones instead.
這家店沒有我尺寸的紅鞋，所以我改買了一雙白色的。
instead of + 名詞／V-ing: Instead of watching TV all afternoon, you should go outside and ride your bike with your friends in the park.
與其整個下午看電視，你應該出去和朋友在公園騎腳踏車。
The bus will not come for another thirty minutes, so let's walk instead and enjoy the nice weather.
公車還要三十分鐘才會來，所以我們改成走路吧，順便享受好天氣。
Walk instead of driving when the store is near your house, because it is good for your health and the air.
當商店離你家很近時，走路而不要開車，因為這對你的健康和空氣都好。
just now: Your mother called just now and asked you to buy some eggs and milk on your way home from school.
你媽媽剛才打電話來，要你放學回家路上買一些雞蛋和牛奶。
just then: I was looking for my umbrella at the door, and just then it stopped raining and the sun came out.
我正在門口找雨傘，就在那時雨停了，太陽出來了。
just in time: We ran to the station as fast as we could and got there just in time to catch the last train.
我們盡快跑到車站，正好及時趕上最後一班火車。
just a minute: Please wait here just a minute while I go upstairs and get my jacket, and then we can leave for the movie.
請在這裡稍等一下，我上樓拿夾克，然後我們就可以出發去看電影了。
just a little: This soup needs just a little salt, so do not add too much, or it will taste too strong.
這湯只要加一點點鹽，所以不要加太多，否則味道會太重。
just about: I am just about finished with my science report, so give me five more minutes and then we can play.
我的自然報告差不多快完成了，所以再給我五分鐘，然後我們就可以玩了。
just like: My little brother looks just like my father when he laughs, and everyone in the family says the same thing.
我弟弟笑的時候就像我爸爸，家裡每個人都這麼說。
just kidding: I told my sister that I ate all her chocolate, but then I laughed and said I was just kidding.
我跟姊姊說我把她的巧克力全吃光了，但接著我笑著說我只是開玩笑的。
just in case: The sky is clear right now, but you should take an umbrella just in case it rains in the afternoon.
現在天空很晴朗，但你應該帶把雨傘以防萬一下午下雨。
just the same: I ordered the chicken and my friend ordered the fish, but the two dishes tasted just the same to me.
我點了雞肉，我朋友點了魚，但這兩道菜對我來說吃起來一樣。
just right: The water in the bath is just right, not too hot and not too cold, so you can get in now.
浴缸的水溫剛剛好，不會太熱也不會太冷，所以你現在可以進去了。
not just: Exercise is not just good for your body; it also helps you feel happy and sleep better at night.
運動不只是對身體好；它也幫助你心情愉快，晚上睡得更好。
just because: My brother bought the expensive shoes just because his favorite basketball player wears the same ones on TV.
我哥哥買那雙昂貴的鞋子，只因為他最喜歡的籃球選手在電視上穿同一款。
just as: Just as I was leaving the house for school, my mother called me back because I forgot my lunch box.
正當我要離開家去上學時，媽媽把我叫回來，因為我忘了帶便當。
just（剛剛；完成式）: I have just finished my homework, so now I can watch my favorite TV show with my little brother.
我剛剛寫完功課，所以現在可以和弟弟一起看我最喜歡的電視節目了。
just now（剛才；過去式）: The teacher came into the room just now, so please be quiet and open your books to page ten.
老師剛才走進教室了，所以請安靜，把書翻到第十頁。
I have just eaten a big bowl of beef noodles, so I do not want any cake right now, thank you.
我剛吃過一大碗牛肉麵，所以我現在不想吃蛋糕，謝謝。
I ate just now at the night market with my cousins, so I am too full to have dinner with you.
我剛才在夜市和表兄弟姊妹吃過了，所以我太飽了，沒辦法和你一起吃晚餐。
only（只有）: Only students in the third grade can join the trip to the museum, so my little sister just has to stay home.
只有三年級的學生可以參加博物館之旅，所以我妹妹只能待在家。
just one more: These cookies are so good that I want just one more, and then I promise I will stop eating them.
這些餅乾太好吃了，我只要再一個，然後我保證就不吃了。
at last: After we waited for two long hours in the cold wind, the last bus to Taipei came at last.
我們在冷風中等了漫長的兩小時後，最後一班往台北的公車終於來了。
last night: Last night my family went to the night market, and we ate fried chicken and played some games there.
昨晚我們全家去了夜市，我們在那裡吃了炸雞還玩了一些遊戲。
last but not least: I want to thank my teachers, my friends, and last but not least, my parents for helping me this year.
我要感謝我的老師、朋友，最後但同樣重要的，我的父母，感謝他們今年對我的幫助。
the last thing I want: The last thing I want on a rainy Monday morning is a big math test, but we have one at eight.
在下雨的星期一早上，我最不想要的就是一場大考，但我們八點就有一場數學考試。
last of all: First we visited the temple, then we had lunch near the river, and last of all we went shopping downtown.
我們先參觀了廟，然後在河邊吃午餐，最後我們去市中心購物。
last time: Last time we went to this restaurant, the service was slow, so let's try the new one across the street.
上次我們來這家餐廳時服務很慢，所以我們試試對街那家新開的吧。
at the last minute: Jack always does his homework at the last minute, so he often makes mistakes and gets a low grade.
傑克總是在最後一刻才寫功課，所以他常常出錯，拿到低分。
the last person to: Amy is the last person to be late for school because she always gets up at six and leaves early.
艾咪是最不可能上學遲到的人，因為她總是六點起床，很早出門。
last（上一個；最後）: I did not watch the last part of the show, so please do not tell me what happened in it.
我沒看這個節目的上一集，所以請不要告訴我裡面發生了什麼事。
latest（最新的）: My brother always wants the latest phone, but the one he bought last year still works well enough for school.
我哥哥總是想要最新的手機，但他去年買的那支對上學來說還夠好用。
the last page: You can find the answers to all the questions on the last page of the book, so check them yourself.
你可以在書的最後一頁找到所有問題的答案，所以自己對一下吧。
last week: Last week we had three tests in two days, so everyone in my class was tired and went to bed early.
上週我們兩天內考了三次試，所以我們班每個人都很累，早早上床睡覺。
the latest news: My grandfather turns on the radio every morning because he wants the latest news, not the news from last night.
我爺爺每天早上打開收音機，因為他想聽最新消息，而不是昨晚的新聞。
stay up late: If you stay up late to play video games every night, you will feel tired and sleepy in class the next day.
如果你每天晚上熬夜玩電動，隔天上課你會覺得又累又睏。
late at night: My father often comes home late at night, so my mother keeps his dinner warm in the kitchen for him.
我爸爸常常深夜才回家，所以我媽媽會在廚房幫他把晚餐保溫。
sleep late: On Sunday mornings I like to sleep late, and then my mother makes a big breakfast for the whole family.
星期天早上我喜歡睡到很晚，然後媽媽會為全家做一頓豐盛的早餐。
run late: Hurry up, we are running late, and the train to Taichung leaves in only fifteen minutes from now.
快一點，我們快遲到了，去台中的火車十五分鐘後就要開了。
work late: My mother had to work late at the office yesterday, so my father cooked dinner for my sister and me.
我媽媽昨天必須在辦公室工作到很晚，所以我爸爸煮晚餐給我和姊姊吃。
late for school: Tom was late for school again today because his alarm clock did not ring and he missed the first bus.
湯姆今天又上學遲到了，因為他的鬧鐘沒響，他錯過了第一班公車。
better late than never: Mark started learning to swim at the age of forty, and he always says better late than never.
馬克四十歲才開始學游泳，他總是說遲做總比不做好。
of late: My grandmother has not been feeling well of late, so we visit her every weekend and bring her favorite fruit.
我奶奶最近身體不太好，所以我們每個週末都去看她，帶她最愛吃的水果。
in late May: Our school trip to the beach will be in late May, when the weather is warm but not too hot.
我們去海邊的學校旅行會在五月下旬，那時天氣溫暖但不會太熱。
late in life: My grandfather started to paint late in life, but now his beautiful pictures hang on the walls of our living room.
我爺爺晚年才開始畫畫，但現在他美麗的畫作掛在我們客廳的牆上。
late（晚；遲）: The movie started late because of a problem with the lights, so we did not get home until eleven.
電影因為燈光出了問題而延遲開始，所以我們直到十一點才到家。
lately（最近）: My cousin has been very busy lately, so she has not had time to come over and play with us.
我表姊最近很忙，所以她沒時間過來和我們一起玩。
come home late: If you come home late again without calling, your parents will be very worried and maybe a little angry.
如果你再次沒打電話就晚回家，你的父母會非常擔心，也許還會有點生氣。
I've been busy lately with homework and basketball practice, so I have not watched any movies this month.
我最近忙著寫功課和練籃球，所以這個月我還沒看過任何電影。
later（之後）: Let us eat lunch first, and later we can go to the park and ride our bicycles along the river.
我們先吃午餐，之後再去公園沿著河邊騎腳踏車吧。
the late Mr. Wang: The school library is named after the late Mr. Wang, who taught English here for more than thirty years.
學校圖書館是以已故的王先生命名的，他在這裡教了三十多年的英文。
What have you done lately?: What have you done lately? I have not seen you at the basketball court for almost a month.
你最近做了什麼？我幾乎一個月沒在籃球場看到你了。
lately 常與完成式連用: Have you seen him lately? He has not come to class for a week, and I am worried about him.
你最近見過他嗎？他一週沒來上課了，我很擔心他。
not lately: I used to swim every morning before school, but not lately, because the weather has been too cold and rainy.
我以前每天上學前都去游泳，但最近沒有，因為天氣一直太冷又下雨。
only lately: Only lately has my little brother started to enjoy reading, and now he takes a book with him everywhere.
直到最近，我弟弟才開始喜歡閱讀，現在他到哪裡都帶著一本書。
I have to go to my piano lesson now, so see you later at the night market around seven.
我現在得去上鋼琴課了，所以待會七點左右在夜市見。
sooner or later: If you keep eating so much fast food and candy, sooner or later you will get sick and need a doctor.
如果你一直吃這麼多速食和糖果，遲早會生病，需要看醫生。
later on: We will have a short meeting at nine, and later on the teacher will take us to the science museum.
我們九點會開一個簡短的會議，之後老師會帶我們去科學博物館。
two days later: Jack lost his dog in the park on Monday, and two days later a kind woman found it near the river.
傑克星期一在公園弄丟了他的狗，兩天後一位好心的女士在河邊找到了它。
no later than: Please hand in your book report no later than Friday morning, or the teacher will take ten points off your grade.
請不晚於星期五早上交書面報告，否則老師會扣你十分。
later that day: We went to the zoo in the morning, and later that day we had a big dinner at my grandmother's house.
我們早上去了動物園，那天稍晚我們在奶奶家吃了一頓豐盛的晚餐。
I have to run to catch my bus now, so catch you later at the baseball game this evening.
我現在得跑去趕公車了，所以今晚在棒球賽上晚點見。
later（之後；從過去某點）: Tom moved to Taipei in 2020, and three years later he opened his own small coffee shop near the station.
湯姆在2020年搬到台北，三年後他在車站附近開了自己的小咖啡店。
in two days（兩天後；從現在）: My aunt will fly back from Japan in two days, and she promised to bring us some chocolate and cookies.
我阿姨兩天後會從日本飛回來，她答應帶一些巧克力和餅乾給我們。
a week later: My family moved to Kaohsiung in March, and a week later my brother found a job at a big hotel there.
我們家三月搬到高雄，一週後我哥哥在那裡的一家大飯店找到了工作。
I have to go to Tainan to visit my grandmother this weekend, so see you in two days, not later than Monday.
這個週末我得去台南探望奶奶，所以兩天後見，不會晚於星期一。
after（之後；接時間點）: My brother usually does his homework right after dinner, and later he plays computer games until nine thirty.
我弟弟通常在晚餐之後馬上寫功課，之後他玩電腦遊戲一直到九點半。
at least: The movie starts at seven, so we should leave home at least thirty minutes early to find good seats.
電影七點開始，所以我們至少要提早三十分鐘出門，才能找到好位子。
at least once: Everyone should try to visit the night market in Taipei at least once because the food there is wonderful.
每個人都應該至少去一次台北的夜市，因為那裡的食物很棒。
the least expensive: This small blue bag is the least expensive one in the store, but it still looks very nice.
這個藍色小包包是店裡最便宜的，但它看起來還是很好看。
not in the least: Mary was not in the least afraid of the big dog, and she even put some water in front of it.
瑪麗一點也不怕那隻大狗，她甚至還把一些水放在它面前。
least of all: Nobody wanted to clean the kitchen after the party, least of all my lazy little brother Tom.
派對結束後沒有人想清理廚房，最不想的就是我懶惰的弟弟湯姆。
to say the least: The test was really hard, to say the least, and most students in our class could not finish it.
至少可以這麼說，這次考試真的很難，我們班大部分的學生都沒寫完。
at least（至少）: You need to drink at least eight glasses of water every day when the weather is this hot.
天氣這麼熱的時候，你每天至少需要喝八杯水。
at most（最多）: The small meeting room can hold at most twenty people, so please tell your friends to come early.
這間小會議室最多能容納二十個人，所以請告訴你的朋友早點來。
at least ten: Our teacher asked us to read at least ten English books this summer and write about each one.
老師要我們這個暑假至少讀十本英文書，並寫下每一本的心得。
at most ten: Each student can borrow at most ten books from the school library, and at least one must be in English.
每個學生最多可以從學校圖書館借十本書，而且至少一本必須是英文書。
the least（最少）: Among all the students in my class, Peter has the least homework because he always finishes it at school.
在我班上所有的學生中，彼得的功課最少，因為他總是在學校就寫完了。
turn left: Walk down this street for five minutes and turn left at the bank, and you will see the post office.
沿著這條街走五分鐘，在銀行左轉，你就會看到郵局。
on the left: In our room at school, the windows are on the left and the door is on the right near the teacher's desk.
在我們學校的教室裡，窗戶在左邊，門在右邊靠近老師的桌子。
left over: There was a lot of food left over after the party, so Mom put it in the refrigerator for tomorrow.
派對結束後剩下很多食物，所以媽媽把它們放進冰箱留到明天。
keep left: When you ride your bike on this road, please keep left so the cars can pass you safely.
當你在這條路上騎腳踏車時，請靠左，這樣車子才能安全地超過你。
left-handed: My cousin is left-handed, so she always sits at the end of the table when we eat dinner together.
我表姊是左撇子，所以我們一起吃晚餐時，她總是坐在桌子的尾端。
the left side: The driver asked us to sit on the left side of the bus because we can see the sea from there.
司機請我們坐在公車的左側，因為從那邊可以看到海。
nothing left: When I got to the bakery at six, there was nothing left because all the bread was sold out.
我六點到麵包店的時候，什麼都不剩了，因為所有的麵包都賣完了。
two left: We bought a box of twelve cookies this morning, but now there are only two left for Dad.
我們今天早上買了一盒十二塊餅乾，但現在只剩兩塊給爸爸了。
left（左邊；向左）: Keep walking along the river and then go left at the big tree, and the park is right there.
沿著河邊繼續走，然後在那棵大樹那裡向左轉，公園就在那裡。
left（leave 的過去式）: My sister left for Japan last Monday, and she will stay there with our aunt for two weeks.
我姊姊上週一離開去日本了，她會在那裡和我們的阿姨住兩個星期。
Jack left early because he had a bad headache, so he did not finish the game with us.
傑克因為頭很痛所以提早離開了，因此他沒有和我們把比賽打完。
Turn left here at the corner, and you will find the new ice cream shop next to the bookstore.
在這個轉角這裡左轉，你就會在書店旁邊找到那家新開的冰淇淋店。
only one left: Hurry up and buy the ticket now, because there is only one left for the show this Saturday night.
快點現在就買票吧，因為這週六晚上的表演只剩一張票了。
more or less: The two houses are more or less the same size, but the one near the park costs much more.
這兩間房子大小差不多，但靠近公園的那一間貴很多。
less than ten: The new MRT station is close to my home, so it takes less than ten minutes to walk there.
新的捷運站離我家很近，所以走到那裡花不到十分鐘。
no less than: No less than three hundred people came to the school fair, and they bought all the cookies in one hour.
多達三百人來參加學校園遊會，他們在一小時內就買光了所有餅乾。
less and less: Grandpa reads less and less these days because his eyes get tired easily, so I read the news to him.
爺爺最近讀書讀得越來越少，因為他的眼睛很容易累，所以我念新聞給他聽。
much less: Tom cannot even cook rice, much less make a big dinner for the whole family on his own.
湯姆連煮飯都不會，更不用說自己為全家人做一頓豐盛的晚餐了。
none the less: It rained all day during our trip, but none the less we had a great time at the beach.
我們旅行時下了一整天的雨，但我們仍然在海邊玩得很開心。
eat less: The doctor asked my father to eat less and walk more because he is a little heavy now.
醫生請我爸爸要少吃多走路，因為他現在有點重了。
in less than a week: Our new puppy learned to sit and come when we call in less than a week, which surprised everyone.
我們的新小狗不到一週就學會坐下和聽到叫就過來，這讓每個人都很驚訝。
less（較少；不可數）: You should put less sugar in the tea because too much sugar is not good for your health.
你應該在茶裡放較少的糖，因為太多糖對你的健康不好。
fewer（較少；可數）: There are fewer students in our class this year, so there is less noise and the teacher is happy.
今年我們班的學生較少，所以噪音較少，老師很開心。
less water: Please use less water when you wash the dishes, because the city does not have much rain this year.
洗碗時請用較少的水，因為今年這個城市沒有很多雨。
fewer people: Fewer people go to the old movie theater now, so it makes less money than before and may close soon.
現在去那間老電影院的人較少，所以它賺的錢比以前少，可能很快就會關門。
less + 形容詞: This math problem is less difficult than the last one, so I think you can finish it alone.
這道數學題比上一題較不困難，所以我想你可以自己把它寫完。
less important: Getting a high score is less important than learning something new, so do not worry about the test.
拿到高分比學到新東西較不重要，所以不要為考試擔心。
no longer: My grandmother no longer lives in the country because she moved to Taipei to be close to us.
我奶奶不再住在鄉下了，因為她搬到台北來好離我們近一點。
so long: It was fun to play basketball with you this afternoon, so long and see you at school tomorrow.
今天下午和你打籃球很開心，再見，明天學校見。
long ago: Long ago, there were no cars or buses in this town, and people walked everywhere or used horses.
很久以前，這個鎮上沒有汽車或公車，人們到哪裡都走路或用馬代步。
take long: It did not take long to cook the noodles, so dinner was ready before Dad came home from work.
煮麵沒有花很久，所以在爸爸下班回家之前晚餐就準備好了。
not long after: Not long after we got to the park, it started to rain, and we had to run back home.
我們到公園不久之後就開始下雨了，我們只好跑回家。
long for: During the long hot summer, the kids long for a cold ice cream and a swim in the sea.
在漫長炎熱的夏天裡，孩子們渴望一支冰涼的冰淇淋和到海裡游個泳。
at long last: After waiting for almost two hours in the rain, the bus came at long last and we got on quickly.
在雨中等了快兩個小時以後，公車終於來了，我們很快地上了車。
How long…?: How long does it take to get to the airport from here by bus on a Sunday morning?
星期天早上從這裡搭公車到機場要花多久？
How long have you been here?: How long have you been here in Taiwan, and do you like the food and the hot weather?
你來台灣這裡多久了？你喜歡這裡的食物和炎熱的天氣嗎？
as long as you want: You can stay at our house as long as you want, because my parents really enjoy talking with you.
只要你想，你可以在我們家住多久都可以，因為我爸媽真的很喜歡和你聊天。
Please wait here for a moment because it won't take long for the doctor to see your little brother.
請在這裡等一下，因為醫生看你弟弟不會花太久。
not any longer: My uncle does not smoke any longer because the doctor said it was very bad for his heart.
我叔叔不再抽菸了，因為醫生說那對他的心臟很不好。
out loud: The teacher asked Lisa to read the poem out loud so that everyone in the class could hear it.
老師請麗莎把那首詩大聲念出來，好讓班上每個人都聽得到。
read out loud: Every morning before school, I read out loud an English story for ten minutes to practice my speaking.
每天早上上學前，我大聲朗讀一篇英文故事十分鐘來練習口說。
laugh out loud: When my dad told that funny joke about the cat, we all began to laugh out loud at the dinner table.
當爸爸講那個關於貓的有趣笑話時，我們全都在餐桌上放聲大笑起來。
think out loud: Sorry, I was just thinking out loud about where to go for lunch, so you do not have to answer me.
抱歉，我只是在邊想邊說午餐要去哪裡吃，所以你不用回答我。
loud and clear: The coach said loud and clear that anyone who comes late to practice will not play in Saturday's game.
教練清楚明白地說，任何練習遲到的人都不能參加星期六的比賽。
loud（大聲地；口語）: Do not play your music so loud at night because the people living next door need to sleep.
晚上不要把音樂放得那麼大聲，因為住隔壁的人需要睡覺。
talk loud: Grandpa cannot hear very well, so you have to talk loud when you want to tell him something.
爺爺聽不太清楚，所以當你想告訴他事情時必須大聲講。
speak loudly: The students in the back of the room could not hear, so the teacher asked Tom to speak loudly.
教室後面的學生聽不到，所以老師請湯姆大聲說。
lie low: After he broke the window with his ball, Peter decided to lie low for a few days at home.
用球打破窗戶之後，彼得決定在家保持低調幾天。
low in fat: This fish is low in fat and full of good things, so my mother cooks it two times a week.
這種魚低脂又營養豐富，所以我媽媽一個星期煮兩次。
run low on: We often run low on milk and eggs by Friday, so I stop by the store on my way home from school.
我們到星期五常常牛奶和蛋快用完，所以我放學回家的路上會去店裡一下。
feel low: Sandy felt low after she lost the singing game, so her friends took her out for some ice cream.
珊蒂在歌唱比賽輸了以後心情低落，所以她的朋友帶她出去吃冰淇淋。
keep the price low: The shop keeps the price low on vegetables so that families with little money can still eat well.
這家店把蔬菜的價格壓低，好讓錢不多的家庭也能吃得好。
low on money: I am a little low on money this month because I spent too much on comic books and snacks.
我這個月錢有點不夠，因為我在漫畫書和零食上花太多錢了。
speak low: The baby was sleeping in the next room, so we had to speak low while we watched the movie.
寶寶在隔壁房間睡覺，所以我們看電影時只能低聲說話。
fly low: Before the big rain, the birds fly low over the farms, and the farmers know the weather will change soon.
大雨來之前，鳥會在農田上低飛，農夫就知道天氣很快要變了。
low（低低地）: The sun hung low in the sky at six o'clock, and the whole beach turned a beautiful orange color.
六點時太陽低低地掛在天空，整個海灘變成了美麗的橘色。
lowly（卑微的）: The old story is about a lowly farm boy who works hard and one day becomes the king's best friend.
這個古老的故事是關於一個卑微的農家男孩，他努力工作，有一天成為國王最好的朋友。
bow low: At the end of the show, all the singers walked to the front of the stage and bowed low to the crowd.
表演結束時，所有歌手走到舞台前方，向觀眾深深鞠躬。
a low voice: My father has a low voice, so when he reads stories at night, my little sister falls asleep quickly.
我爸爸的聲音低沉，所以他晚上念故事時，我的小妹很快就睡著了。
I cannot help you with your math homework right now because I am busy cooking, so maybe later tonight.
我現在不能幫你寫數學功課，因為我正忙著做飯，或許今晚晚點吧。
Do you think it will stop raining before the baseball game this afternoon, or maybe not?
你覺得今天下午棒球比賽前雨會停嗎，還是也許不會？
You say the new restaurant near the station is better than ours, and maybe so, but it costs too much.
你說車站附近的新餐廳比我們的好，也許是這樣，但它太貴了。
maybe someday: I do not have enough money to travel to Japan now, but maybe someday I will see the beautiful flowers there.
我現在沒有足夠的錢去日本旅行，但或許有一天我會在那裡看到美麗的花。
Maybe you're right about the weather, so let us bring an umbrella to the park just in case.
關於天氣或許你是對的，所以我們帶把傘去公園以防萬一吧。
maybe（也許；一字，副詞）: Maybe we can go to the beach on Sunday if the weather is nice and Dad does not have to work.
如果天氣好而且爸爸不用工作，也許我們星期天可以去海邊。
may be（可能是；兩字，動詞）: The restaurant may be closed today because it is a holiday, so maybe we should call before we go.
那家餐廳今天可能是關門的，因為今天是假日，所以也許我們去之前應該先打電話。
Maybe he is sick today, because he usually comes to school early and sits in the front row.
也許他今天病了，因為他通常都很早到學校，坐在前排。
John did not eat anything at lunch, so he may be sick, or maybe he is just worried about the test.
約翰午餐什麼都沒吃，所以他可能病了，或者也許他只是在擔心考試。
perhaps（也許；較正式）: Perhaps we should take the train to Tainan, or maybe the bus, because the roads will be very busy this weekend.
也許我們應該搭火車去台南，或者也許搭公車，因為這個週末路上會非常塞。
more and more: More and more students ride a bike to school now because it is good for their health and the air.
現在越來越多的學生騎腳踏車上學，因為那對他們的健康和空氣都好。
once more: The song was so beautiful that everyone asked the band to play it once more before they went home.
這首歌太美了，所以每個人都要求樂團在回家前再演奏一次。
no more: There is no more rice in the kitchen, so we have to eat noodles for dinner tonight instead.
廚房裡沒有更多的米了，所以我們今晚只好改吃麵當晚餐。
more than: More than five hundred people came to the night market on Saturday to try the famous fried chicken.
星期六有超過五百人來夜市品嚐那有名的炸雞。
what's more: This phone takes great pictures, and what's more, it costs much less than the one I saw yesterday.
這支手機拍照很棒，而且它比我昨天看到的那支便宜很多。
the more…the more: The more Jenny practices the piano after school, the more beautiful her music sounds to the family.
珍妮放學後練鋼琴練得越多，她的音樂在家人聽來就越美。
more than happy to: My aunt is more than happy to drive us to the museum because she loves art and old things too.
我阿姨非常樂意開車送我們去博物館，因為她也很喜歡藝術和古老的東西。
any more: Do you want any more tea or cake before we leave, because there is still a lot on the table?
我們離開前你還想再多一點茶或蛋糕嗎？桌上還有很多。
some more: The soup is really good tonight, Mom, so could I please have some more before my brother finishes it all?
媽，今晚的湯真好喝，可以請妳在弟弟全部喝完以前再給我多一些嗎？
more + 多音節形容詞: For me, English is more interesting than math because I can use it to talk with people from other countries.
對我來說，英文比數學更有趣，因為我可以用它和其他國家的人交談。
more beautiful than: Many people think the flowers in spring are more beautiful than the red leaves we see in the fall.
很多人認為春天的花比我們在秋天看到的紅葉更美。
the more…, the more…: The more my little brother plays video games at night, the more tired he looks in class the next morning.
我弟弟晚上玩電動玩得越多，隔天早上上課時看起來就越累。
The more you read, the more you know, so our teacher gives us a new book every month.
讀得越多，知道得越多，所以我們的老師每個月都給我們一本新書。
more than ten: More than ten students in our class joined the school basketball team this year, which made the coach very happy.
我們班今年有超過十個學生加入學校籃球隊，這讓教練非常開心。
not more than: Students may bring not more than two snacks on the school trip, so choose your favorite ones carefully.
學生在校外教學可以帶不超過兩份零食，所以要小心選擇你最喜歡的。
most of all: I love my new school for many reasons, but most of all I love the kind teachers and friendly students.
我喜歡我的新學校有很多理由，但最重要的是我喜歡親切的老師和友善的學生。
at most: The trip from my house to the train station takes at most fifteen minutes if I walk fast.
如果我走得快，從我家到火車站最多花十五分鐘。
make the most of: We only have three days in Japan, so let us make the most of our time and visit the famous places early.
我們在日本只有三天，所以讓我們善用時間，早點去參觀那些有名的地方。
for the most part: For the most part, the students in my class like the new English teacher because she makes lessons fun.
大部分來說，我班上的學生喜歡新來的英文老師，因為她讓課程變得有趣。
most of the time: My grandfather spends most of the time in his garden, where he grows tomatoes and talks to his birds.
我爺爺大部分時間都待在他的花園裡，在那裡種番茄，和他的鳥說話。
the most important: The most important thing before a test is to get enough sleep, not to study all night long.
考試前最重要的事是睡眠充足，而不是整夜讀書。
most people: Most people in Taiwan drink tea every day, and many of them like it with milk and ice.
台灣大部分的人每天都喝茶，而且很多人喜歡加牛奶和冰。
most of them: I have many friends in this class, and most of them live near the school and walk there together.
我在這個班上有很多朋友，他們大多數住在學校附近，一起走路上學。
most（大部分；最）: Most kids in my town love the summer because they can swim in the river and eat ice cream.
我們鎮上大部分的孩子都愛夏天，因為他們可以在河裡游泳、吃冰淇淋。
mostly（主要地；多半）: The people at the party were mostly my mother's friends from work, so I did not know many of them.
派對上的人主要是我媽媽工作上的朋友，所以我認識的人不多。
most students: Most students in our school take the bus home, but a few of them ride a bike or walk with friends.
我們學校大部分學生搭公車回家，但有少數人騎腳踏車或和朋友一起走路。
the most expensive: That red watch in the window is the most expensive one in the shop, so I can only look at it.
櫥窗裡那支紅色的手錶是店裡最貴的，所以我只能看看。
Students here are mostly from Taipei, but some of them come from small towns in the south and live at school.
這裡的學生多半來自台北，但有些人來自南部的小鎮，住在學校裡。
mostly sunny: The weather report says it will be mostly sunny this weekend, so we can finally have our picnic by the lake.
天氣預報說這個週末大多晴天，所以我們終於可以在湖邊野餐了。
mostly students: The people waiting outside the bookstore at nine were mostly students who wanted to buy the new comic book.
九點時在書店外面等的人多半是想買新漫畫書的學生。
On rainy Sundays I mostly stay home and read or watch movies with my family in the living room.
下雨的星期天我多半待在家，和家人在客廳看書或看電影。
mostly because: I did not join the school trip to the mountain, mostly because I had a bad cold that week.
我沒有參加學校去山上的旅行，主要是因為那週我得了重感冒。
very much: Thank you very much for helping me carry these heavy books all the way to the library this morning.
非常感謝你今天早上幫我把這些很重的書一路搬到圖書館。
too much: My sister puts too much salt in her soup, so nobody at the table wants to try it again.
我姊姊在她的湯裡放了太多鹽，所以餐桌上沒有人想再試一次。
so much: There is so much homework to do tonight that I cannot go to the movies with you after dinner.
今晚有這麼多功課要做，所以晚餐後我不能和你去看電影。
how much: How much is this blue jacket, and do you have a bigger size for my tall older brother?
這件藍色夾克多少錢？你們有給我高大的哥哥穿的更大尺寸嗎？
not much: There is not much milk left in the bottle, so please buy some on your way home from work.
瓶子裡剩的牛奶不多了，所以請你下班回家的路上買一些。
much better: I feel much better today after sleeping for ten hours, so I can go back to school tomorrow.
睡了十個小時後我今天好很多了，所以明天可以回學校上課。
much too hot: It is much too hot to play basketball outside at noon, so let us wait until five o'clock.
中午在外面打籃球實在太熱了，所以我們等到五點吧。
as much as: My little brother can eat as much as my father at dinner, but he is still very thin.
我弟弟晚餐可以吃得和我爸爸一樣多，但他還是很瘦。
much the same: The two restaurants are much the same, but the one near the park has more kinds of ice cream.
這兩家餐廳大致相同，但公園旁的那家有更多種冰淇淋。
much more: Mary enjoys reading much more than watching TV, so she visits the library almost every afternoon after school.
瑪麗喜歡閱讀遠超過看電視，所以她幾乎每天放學後都去圖書館。
much + 比較級: This new bike is much faster than my old one, so now I get to school in ten minutes.
這台新腳踏車比我的舊車快很多，所以現在我十分鐘就能到學校。
much taller than: Tom is much taller than his older sister now, so he has to stand in the back row for photos.
湯姆現在比他姊姊高很多，所以拍照時他得站在後排。
much + 不可數名詞: We did not have much rain this summer, so the farmers are worried about their rice and fruit trees.
我們今年夏天沒有很多雨，所以農夫很擔心他們的稻米和果樹。
much time: Doing all this homework takes much time, so I cannot play basketball with my friends after school today.
做完這些功課花很多時間，所以我今天放學後不能和朋友打籃球。
many + 可數名詞: There are many kinds of fruit at the market, but I do not have much money to buy any.
市場裡有很多種水果，但我沒有很多錢可以買。
too much homework: Our teacher gave us too much homework for the weekend, so I cannot visit my grandmother on Sunday.
我們老師給我們週末太多功課，所以我星期天不能去探望奶奶。
near here: Is there a post office near here, because I need to send this birthday card to my friend in Japan?
這附近有郵局嗎？因為我需要把這張生日卡片寄給我在日本的朋友。
come near: The little cat came near when it smelled the fish, but it ran away when my dog barked.
那隻小貓聞到魚的味道就靠近了，但我的狗一叫，它就跑掉了。
near the end: The movie was boring at first, but near the end there was a big surprise that made everyone cry.
這部電影一開始很無聊，但接近尾聲時有個大驚喜讓每個人都哭了。
in the near future: In the near future, students may use computers for all their tests instead of paper and pencils.
在不久的將來，學生可能會用電腦來做所有的考試，而不用紙和鉛筆。
nowhere near: My drawing of the dog is nowhere near as good as Amy's because she takes art lessons every week.
我畫的狗遠遠不及艾美畫得好，因為她每個星期都上美術課。
near and far: People came from near and far to see the beautiful lanterns in the sky on the night of the festival.
節慶的那個晚上，遠近各處的人都來看天空中美麗的燈籠。
near at hand: I always keep a pencil and some paper near at hand because good ideas often come when I am eating.
我總是把鉛筆和一些紙放在手邊，因為好點子常常在我吃東西時出現。
near（接近；距離）: Our new house is near the MRT station, so my father can get to work in only twenty minutes.
我們的新家接近捷運站，所以我爸爸只要二十分鐘就能到公司。
nearly（幾乎）: I nearly missed the school bus this morning because I could not find my shoes under the bed.
我今天早上幾乎錯過校車，因為我在床底下找不到我的鞋子。
live near the school: Lucy lives near the school, so she can walk home for lunch and come back before the bell rings.
露西住在學校附近，所以她可以走回家吃午餐，然後在鐘響前回來。
nearly finished: My science homework is nearly finished, so I can watch the baseball game with Dad in a few minutes.
我的自然作業幾乎完成了，所以幾分鐘後我就可以和爸爸一起看棒球賽。
near（不加 to）: The new bakery is near my school, so my friends and I often buy bread there after class.
那家新麵包店靠近我的學校，所以我和朋友常常下課後去那裡買麵包。
next to（在旁邊）: Jenny sits next to the window, not just near it, because she likes to feel the warm sun while she reads.
珍妮坐在窗戶旁邊，不只是靠近窗戶，因為她喜歡在閱讀時感受溫暖的陽光。
nearly every day: My grandfather goes to the park nearly every day to walk his dog and talk with his old friends.
我爺爺幾乎每天都去公園遛狗，並和他的老朋友聊天。
nearly ten o'clock: It is nearly ten o'clock, so you should finish your homework quickly and get ready for bed now.
快十點了，所以你應該趕快把功課寫完，現在準備上床睡覺。
nearly fell: Be careful on the wet floor because I nearly fell down this morning when I ran into the kitchen.
小心濕地板，因為我今天早上跑進廚房時差點跌倒。
nearly all: Nearly all the students in our class passed the English test, and the teacher brought us cookies to celebrate.
我們班幾乎全部的學生都通過了英文考試，老師帶了餅乾來幫我們慶祝。
not nearly enough: One bottle of water is not nearly enough for a long hike in the mountains on a hot summer day.
在炎熱的夏天到山上長途健行，一瓶水遠遠不夠。
near（接近）: The bus stop is near the hospital, so you can walk there in two minutes after you see the doctor.
公車站接近醫院，所以你看完醫生後走兩分鐘就可以到那裡。
not nearly（遠遠不）: My brother is not nearly as tall as my father, but he still hopes to play basketball for the school.
我哥哥的身高遠遠不如我爸爸，但他還是希望能加入學校打籃球。
nearly new: My cousin gave me his old phone, and it is nearly new because he only used it for two months.
我表哥把他的舊手機給了我，它幾乎全新，因為他只用了兩個月。
Amy said she does not like ghost movies, and I told her me neither, so we watched a funny one instead.
艾美說她不喜歡鬼片，我告訴她我也不喜歡，所以我們改看了一部好笑的電影。
My brother does not want to go to the night market tonight, and neither do I because it is too hot.
我弟弟今晚不想去夜市，我也不想，因為天氣太熱了。
neither of them: I asked Tom and Peter about the party, but neither of them knew what time it would start on Saturday.
我問了湯姆和彼得關於派對的事，但他們兩個都不知道星期六幾點開始。
neither here nor there: Whether you wear the red shirt or the blue one is neither here nor there, because nobody will notice at the picnic.
你穿紅色還是藍色襯衫無關緊要，因為野餐時沒有人會注意。
neither…nor: The small restaurant near our school is neither cheap nor clean, so my friends and I never eat there.
我們學校附近那家小餐廳既不便宜也不乾淨，所以我和朋友從不去那裡吃飯。
Neither + 助動詞 + 主詞: My father never eats fast food, and neither does my mother, so we always cook dinner together at home.
我爸爸從不吃速食，我媽媽也不吃，所以我們總是一起在家做晚餐。
Lisa cannot swim very well, and neither can I, so we both stayed on the beach and played in the sand.
麗莎游泳游得不太好，我也不會，所以我們兩個都留在沙灘上玩沙。
I did not finish the math homework last night because it was so hard, and neither did she.
昨晚我沒有寫完數學功課，因為它太難了，她也沒有。
Lisa loves playing basketball after school, and so do I, but neither of us likes to run in the hot sun.
麗莎喜歡放學後打籃球，我也是，但我們兩個都不喜歡在大太陽下跑步。
neither…nor 動詞看靠近者: Neither the students nor the teacher knows the answer to this question, so we will look it up in the library.
學生和老師都不知道這個問題的答案，所以我們會去圖書館查。
Neither he nor I am wrong about the time of the game, because the coach changed it twice this week.
關於比賽時間，他和我都沒錯，因為教練這星期改了兩次。
never mind: Never mind about the cup you dropped, because it was old and I can buy a new one at the store.
別介意你摔掉的那個杯子，因為它舊了，我可以去店裡買一個新的。
never ever: I will never ever ride that terrible fast train at the park again, even if you give me free tickets.
我絕對不會再坐遊樂園那個可怕的快車，就算你給我免費票也不要。
Never say never, because my grandmother started to learn English at seventy and now she reads stories in English.
永不說不可能，因為我奶奶七十歲開始學英文，現在她能讀英文故事了。
never too late: It is never too late to learn to swim, so my father joined a class at the pool last month.
學游泳永遠不嫌晚，所以我爸爸上個月在泳池報名了一個班。
You never know, maybe your favorite singer will come to our school festival this year and sing for us.
誰知道呢，也許你最喜歡的歌手今年會來我們的學校慶典為我們唱歌。
never 放一般動詞前: My mother never drinks coffee after six in the evening because it makes it hard for her to sleep.
我媽媽晚上六點以後從不喝咖啡，因為那會讓她很難入睡。
never 放 be 動詞後: The food in this restaurant is never cold when it comes to the table, so we eat here every Friday.
這家餐廳的食物送上桌時從來不會是冷的，所以我們每個星期五都來這裡吃。
I never eat breakfast at home on school days because I always get up late and have to run to school.
上學日我從不在家吃早餐，因為我總是晚起，必須跑著去學校。
Our math teacher is never late for class, and he always comes in with a big smile and a cup of tea.
我們的數學老師上課從不遲到，他總是帶著大大的笑容和一杯茶走進來。
Never give up!: Never give up, even when the game looks lost, because our team won last year in the last two minutes.
永不放棄，就算比賽看起來快輸了，因為我們的隊伍去年在最後兩分鐘贏了。
never 不與 not 連用: Jack never comes to practice on time, and the coach is not happy about it, so Jack may not play on Sunday.
傑克從不準時來練習，教練對此很不高興，所以傑克星期天可能不能上場。
next to: The new bakery is next to the bank on Green Street, and it sells very good egg cakes and bread.
那家新麵包店在綠街的銀行旁邊，它賣很好吃的蛋糕和麵包。
next time: I did not have time to visit the museum today, but next time I come to Taipei, I will go there first.
我今天沒有時間去參觀博物館，但下次我來台北時，我會先去那裡。
next door: The old man who lives next door grows beautiful flowers in his garden and gives some to my mother every spring.
住在隔壁的老先生在他的花園裡種美麗的花，每年春天都送一些給我媽媽。
the next day: We arrived in Tainan late at night, and the next day we got up early to eat the famous breakfast there.
我們深夜抵達台南，第二天我們早起去吃那裡有名的早餐。
next week: There is a big English test next week, so I plan to study with my friends at the library every night.
下週有一場大的英文考試，所以我打算每天晚上和朋友在圖書館讀書。
what next?: We have finished at the market and had lunch there, so what next, a movie or a walk in the park?
我們已經逛完市場，也在那裡吃了午餐，接下來呢？看電影還是去公園散步？
next to nothing: My little brother knows next to nothing about cooking, but he still wants to make dinner for Mom's birthday.
我弟弟對做菜幾乎一無所知，但他還是想在媽媽生日時做晚餐。
next in line: Please wait on the chair outside the office, because you are next in line to see the school nurse.
請在辦公室外面的椅子上等，因為你是下一位要見校護的人。
next（下一個；從現在）: We are going to Japan next summer, so I am studying a little Japanese every day after school this year.
我們明年夏天要去日本，所以我今年每天放學後都學一點日文。
the next（接著的；從過去）: My aunt came to stay with us in June, and the next month she found a job near our house.
我阿姨六月來和我們住，接著的那個月她在我們家附近找到了工作。
next Monday: The school basketball game is next Monday, so our team will practice every afternoon this week after class.
學校的籃球比賽在下週一，所以我們隊這週每天下午下課後都會練習。
the next Monday: Peter moved to Taipei in the spring, and the next Monday he started school and made two new friends.
彼得春天搬到台北，接下來的週一他就開始上學，並交了兩個新朋友。
the following day: It rained hard on the first day of our trip, but the following day, not the next one, was sunny and warm.
我們旅行的第一天下大雨，但隔天，不是再下一天，是晴朗溫暖的。
no way: No way am I going to eat that strange green soup, because it smells like old fish and dirty socks.
我絕不會吃那碗奇怪的綠色湯，因為它聞起來像臭掉的魚和髒襪子。
no doubt: No doubt Jenny will win the singing game again this year, because she practices two hours every day.
珍妮今年無疑會再贏得歌唱比賽，因為她每天練習兩小時。
no wonder: You ate three bowls of noodles and two pieces of cake at lunch, so no wonder you feel so full.
你午餐吃了三碗麵和兩塊蛋糕，難怪你覺得這麼飽。
no problem: No problem, I can help you carry the boxes to your new apartment on Saturday because I am free all day.
沒問題，我星期六可以幫你把箱子搬到你的新公寓，因為我整天都有空。
No kidding!: No kidding! You really met the famous baseball player at the night market and he signed your cap?
不是開玩笑吧！你真的在夜市遇到那位有名的棒球員，而且他還在你的帽子上簽名？
No matter what: No matter what happens in the game tomorrow, our class will cheer for the team from the start to the end.
不管明天比賽發生什麼事，我們班都會從頭到尾為球隊加油。
say no to: It is hard to say no to a second piece of chocolate cake, but I am trying to eat healthy food this month.
要拒絕第二塊巧克力蛋糕很難，但我這個月正努力吃健康的食物。
no more than: The walk from the train station to my school takes no more than ten minutes, so I never need the bus.
從火車站走到我學校只有不過十分鐘，所以我從來不需要搭公車。
no + 比較級: This new phone is no cheaper than the old one, so I will keep using mine until it stops working.
這支新手機並不比舊的便宜，所以我會繼續用我的，直到它壞掉。
no better than: My cooking is no better than my brother's, so our parents still make dinner for us every night.
我的廚藝不比我弟弟好，所以我們的父母每天晚上還是為我們做晚餐。
no sooner…than…: No sooner had we sat down for the picnic than it started to rain, so we ran back to the car.
我們一坐下來野餐，天就開始下雨了，所以我們跑回車上。
There is no telling what the weather will be like on Sunday, so bring a jacket and an umbrella just in case.
不可能知道星期天天氣會怎樣，所以帶件夾克和一把雨傘以防萬一。
no + 名詞: There is no milk in the refrigerator this morning, so we have to drink juice with our bread.
今天早上冰箱裡沒有牛奶，所以我們只能配果汁吃麵包。
The sign on the wall says No smoking, so my uncle had to go outside to the street to smoke.
牆上的標示寫著禁止吸菸，所以我叔叔只好到外面街上抽菸。
right now: The typhoon is coming, so Dad asked us to close all the windows right now before the strong wind arrives.
颱風要來了，所以爸爸要我們在強風到達之前現在立刻把所有窗戶關好。
now and then: My grandmother lives in Tainan, and we take the train to visit her now and then on long weekends.
我奶奶住在台南，我們偶爾會在長週末搭火車去看她。
from now on: After I failed the math test, I promised my mother that I would study harder from now on.
數學考試不及格之後，我向媽媽保證從現在起我會更用功讀書。
by now: The movie started an hour ago, so by now Tom and his friends should already be in their seats in the theater.
電影一小時前就開始了，所以到現在湯姆和他的朋友們應該已經在電影院的座位上了。
up to now: Up to now, our basketball team has won every game this season, and we are very proud of that.
到目前為止，我們籃球隊這一季每場比賽都贏了，我們對此感到非常驕傲。
for now: We do not have enough money for a new sofa, so for now we will keep using the old one.
我們沒有足夠的錢買新沙發，所以目前我們會暫時繼續用舊的。
now that: Now that the rain has stopped, let's go to the park and play badminton before dinner.
既然雨已經停了，我們晚餐前去公園打羽球吧。
Now what?: We missed the last bus home, and my little brother looked at me and asked, Now what?
我們錯過了回家的最後一班公車，弟弟看著我問：現在怎麼辦？
any day now: The mangoes on the tree are almost yellow, so Grandpa says we can pick them any day now.
樹上的芒果快變黃了，所以爺爺說我們隨時都可以採了，就在這幾天。
now（現在）: Mary is studying English in her room now, so please do not play the drum so loudly.
瑪麗現在正在房間裡讀英文，所以請不要那麼大聲打鼓。
just now（剛才）: Just now I met our teacher in the supermarket, and she was buying a lot of apples and milk.
我剛才在超市遇到我們的老師，她正在買很多蘋果和牛奶。
right now（馬上）: The soup is boiling over on the stove, so turn off the fire right now before it makes the kitchen dirty.
湯在爐子上滾出來了，所以馬上把火關掉，不然廚房會弄得很髒。
now that + 子句（既然）: Now that you have finished all your homework, you may watch TV for half an hour before bed.
既然你已經做完所有功課，睡前可以看半小時電視。
day off: Friday is my mother's day off, so she usually takes us to the night market for dinner.
星期五是媽媽的休假日，所以她通常會帶我們去夜市吃晚餐。
take off: Our plane will take off at nine, so we have to arrive at the airport before seven in the morning.
我們的飛機九點起飛，所以我們早上七點前就得到機場。
turn off: Please turn off the lights and the air conditioner when you leave the room to save energy.
離開房間時請把燈和冷氣關掉，以節省能源。
put off: Because of the heavy rain, the school decided to put off the sports day until next Wednesday.
因為下大雨，學校決定把運動會延期到下星期三。
get off: You should get off the bus at the next stop, and then the library is right across the street.
你應該在下一站下車，然後圖書館就在對街。
show off: Jack likes to show off his new cellphone to everyone, but nobody in our class really cares.
傑克喜歡向大家炫耀他的新手機，但班上沒有人真的在意。
call off: The teacher had to call off the picnic because a strong typhoon was coming to Taiwan that weekend.
老師不得不取消野餐，因為那個週末有強烈颱風要來台灣。
go off: My alarm clock did not go off this morning, so I was late for school for the first time.
我的鬧鐘今天早上沒有響起，所以我第一次上學遲到。
set off: We will set off for the mountains at six tomorrow morning, so please go to bed early tonight.
我們明天早上六點要出發去山上，所以今晚請早點睡。
be off: It is already ten o'clock, and I must be off now because my mother is waiting for me outside.
已經十點了，我現在必須離開，因為我媽媽在外面等我。
off and on: It rained off and on all afternoon, so we stayed inside and played cards with our cousins.
整個下午斷斷續續地下著雨，所以我們待在屋裡和表兄弟姊妹玩牌。
see sb. off: My uncle is moving to Japan for work, so the whole family drove to the airport to see him off.
我叔叔要搬去日本工作，所以全家人都開車到機場為他送行。
off duty: My father is a police officer, and when he is off duty, he likes to go fishing by the river.
我爸爸是警察，他下班的時候喜歡去河邊釣魚。
10% off: This jacket is 10% off this week, so I think I will buy it before the sale ends on Sunday.
這件夾克這星期打九折，所以我想在星期天特賣結束前買下來。
far off: Summer vacation seems far off when you are taking exams, but it will be here before you know it.
當你在考試的時候，暑假似乎很遙遠，但它會在你還沒察覺前就到來。
keep off the grass: The sign in the park says keep off the grass, so we played frisbee on the basketball court instead.
公園裡的牌子寫著勿踐踏草坪，所以我們改在籃球場上玩飛盤。
how often: How often do you go to the library after school, and what kind of books do you usually borrow?
你放學後多常去圖書館，你通常借哪一類的書？
every so often: My grandfather does not use the internet much, but every so often he sends us a short email.
我爺爺不太用網路，但他偶爾會寄一封短短的電子郵件給我們。
more often than not: More often than not, my little sister falls asleep on the sofa before the movie is even half over.
多半的時候，我妹妹在電影還沒播到一半就在沙發上睡著了。
as often as possible: The doctor asked my father to walk as often as possible because he sits in the office all day.
醫生告訴我爸爸要盡量多走路，因為他整天坐在辦公室裡。
quite often: We eat at the noodle shop near the school quite often because the food is cheap and delicious.
我們相當常在學校附近的麵店吃飯，因為那裡的食物便宜又好吃。
not often: It does not often snow in Taiwan, so many people drive up the mountains when it finally does.
台灣不常下雪，所以當終於下雪時，很多人會開車上山。
How often do you…?: How often do you call your grandfather, and does he still remember all of your friends' names?
你多常打電話給爺爺，他還記得你所有朋友的名字嗎？
How often do you exercise?: How often do you exercise every week, and do you like to run outside or swim in the pool more?
你每週多常運動，你比較喜歡在外面跑步還是在泳池游泳？
once a week: I have a piano lesson once a week, and my teacher often gives me a new song to practice at home.
我每週上一次鋼琴課，老師常常給我一首新歌在家練習。
often 放一般動詞前: Our class often plays basketball after school, and we sometimes stay at the playground until dark.
我們班常常在放學後打籃球，有時候會在操場待到天黑。
often 放 be 動詞後: The buses are often late during rush hour, so I leave home twenty minutes early on school days.
尖峰時間公車常常會晚到，所以上學的日子我會提早二十分鐘出門。
at once: When the teacher noticed the smoke in the kitchen, she asked all the students to leave the building at once.
老師注意到廚房有煙時，馬上叫所有學生離開大樓。
once upon a time: Once upon a time, a kind farmer lived with his three daughters in a small village near the sea.
很久很久以前，一位善良的農夫和他的三個女兒住在海邊的一個小村子裡。
once in a while: My family likes to eat at home, but once in a while we go to a nice restaurant to celebrate.
我家喜歡在家吃飯，但偶爾我們會去一家好餐廳慶祝。
once and for all: Let's clean out the garage once and for all this weekend so we never have to look at all that trash again.
這個週末我們一次把車庫徹底清理乾淨吧，這樣就再也不用看到那些垃圾了。
for once: My brother always chooses the movie, so for once I would like to pick the one we watch tonight.
我哥哥總是負責選電影，所以就這一次，我想挑今晚我們要看的那一部。
once + 子句（一旦）: Once you learn how to ride a bicycle, you will never forget it, even after many years.
一旦你學會騎腳踏車，即使過了很多年你也不會忘記。
Once you start reading this comic book, do not stop, because the story gets more exciting with every page.
一旦你開始讀這本漫畫，就別停下來，因為故事隨著每一頁越來越精彩。
once（曾經）: My grandfather once worked as a sailor, and he still tells us exciting stories about the ocean.
我爺爺曾經當過水手，他現在還會跟我們說關於海洋的精彩故事。
Mr. Lin once lived in this old house by the river before he moved to Taipei for a new job.
林先生曾經住在河邊這間老房子裡，後來才搬到台北找新工作。
once or twice: I have only been to the new department store once or twice, so I do not know where the bookstore is.
我只去過新的百貨公司一兩次，所以不知道書店在哪裡。
only child: Amy is an only child, so she often invites her cousins over to play because the house feels quiet.
艾咪是獨生女，所以她常邀表兄弟姊妹來家裡玩，因為家裡感覺很安靜。
if only: If only I had studied harder last night, I would not feel so nervous about the English test now.
要是我昨晚更用功一點就好了，現在就不會對英文考試這麼緊張了。
only too happy: When my neighbor asked me to walk her dog, I said I would be only too happy to help her.
當鄰居請我幫她遛狗時，我說我非常樂意幫忙。
only just: The bus arrived just as I reached the stop, so I only just caught it and did not have to wait.
公車在我剛到站牌時到了，所以我剛好勉強趕上，不用等。
the only way: The only way to get a good grade in science is to review your notes a little bit every day.
想在自然科拿到好成績，唯一的方法就是每天複習一點筆記。
only yesterday: It was only yesterday that I lent you my dictionary, so how could you lose it so quickly?
我就在昨天才把字典借給你，你怎麼可能這麼快就弄丟了？
for kids only: This small swimming pool at the park is for kids only, so adults have to use the big one next to it.
公園裡這座小泳池僅限小孩使用，所以大人要用旁邊那座大的。
Only + 副詞子句 + 倒裝: Only after the teacher explained the question twice did the whole class understand how to solve it.
直到老師把題目解釋了兩次之後，全班才明白要怎麼解。
Only then did I understand why my mother wanted me to bring an umbrella to school that morning.
直到那時我才明白，為什麼那天早上媽媽要我帶雨傘去學校。
Only when it rains do we stay home on Sunday; on sunny days we always ride our bicycles to the river.
只有下雨時我們星期天才待在家；天氣好的時候我們總是騎腳踏車去河邊。
Not only…but also + 倒裝: Not only did Tom win the race, but he also helped a runner who fell down near the finish line.
湯姆不但贏了賽跑，還幫了一位在終點線附近跌倒的跑者。
Not only is he smart, but he is also kin: Not only is my sister smart, but she is also kind to everyone, so all the teachers like her a lot.
我姊姊不但聰明，而且對每個人都很善良，所以所有老師都很喜歡她。
only + 修飾位置改變意思: I only ate one cookie, but my brother only ate cookies, so he had no room for dinner at all.
我只吃了一片餅乾，但我哥哥只吃餅乾，所以他完全沒有胃口吃晚餐。
watch out: Watch out for the cars when you cross the street, because the drivers here do not always stop.
過馬路時要小心車子，因為這裡的駕駛不一定會停下來。
find out: I want to find out who left this beautiful birthday card on my desk this morning before class.
我想查明今天早上上課前是誰把這張漂亮的生日卡放在我桌上。
figure out: It took me an hour to figure out this math problem, but I felt great when I finally got the answer.
我花了一個小時才想出這道數學題，但終於算出答案時我覺得棒極了。
run out of: We ran out of milk this morning, so I had to eat my cereal with juice, and it tasted terrible.
我們今天早上牛奶用完了，所以我只好用果汁配麥片吃，味道糟透了。
turn out: Everyone was afraid of the big dog next door, but it turned out to be very friendly and gentle.
大家都怕隔壁的大狗，但結果它非常友善又溫和。
eat out: My parents are both too tired to cook on Fridays, so our family usually eats out at a noodle shop.

outside the box: Our teacher asked us to think outside the box, so our group made a robot out of old paper boxes.

孩子們喜歡晚餐後在外面玩，天空變黑了才回家。
outside（在外面；不加 of）: My bicycle is right outside the school gate, so we can ride together to the night market after class.

get over: It took my grandmother two weeks to get over her cold, and now she is finally strong enough to go out again.

over there: The bookstore is over there, next to the bakery with the big red sign, so you cannot miss it.

overseas students: There are many overseas students in my uncle's university, and some of them come from Japan and Korea.

an overseas trip: This summer my family is making plans for an overseas trip to Japan, and I am so excited about riding the fast trains.

work overseas: My father has to work overseas for six months, so we talk to him on the computer every weekend.

from overseas: The new teacher comes from overseas, and she loves to tell us stories about her home city in America.

overseas（海外；不加 to）: Many young people in Taiwan want to go overseas to study or work, but they often miss their families.

abroad（國外）: My older brother went abroad to study last September, and living overseas has taught him to cook for himself.
我哥哥去年九月去國外讀書，在海外生活教會了他自己煮飯。
foreign（外國的）: Learning a foreign language is useful, because when you travel overseas you can make friends from different countries.

a foreign country: I have never visited a foreign country, so I am very excited about our first overseas trip to Japan next month.
